title: A Drop for the Border
premise: Jonah Reyes, a private security contractor who guards clients nobody trusts, receives a debt notice from a stranger claiming she owes a favor that never happened — a favor tied to the black-site program that trained her before erasing her records. The stranger, Marisol, is a survivor of the same program, and repaying the 'interest' means helping her expose the network that manufactured operatives like them. As Jonah digs into buried identities and old handlers resurface to silence Marisol, she discovers her own erased past is the key evidence, and that the network's founder is the man she's been guarding for years. In the end, Jonah burns the program's archives at the cost of her cover, her livelihood, and nearly her life — surviving with no name but the one she chooses for herself.
about_author: Felix Vasquez is the pen name of a former security consultant who spent a decade working border-adjacent contracts across the Southwest before turning to fiction. He writes thrillers about people whose jobs require them to be unmemorable.

chapters.title: The Favor That Never Happened
chapters.summary: Jonah Reyes, POV. Between contracts in El Paso, Jonah receives an envelope containing photos of herself in places she has no memory of, plus a note: one favor owed, interest accruing. She sweeps her apartment and finds nothing — which frightens her more than the photos. Emotional beat: controlled unease cracking into genuine fear.

chapters.title: Clients Nobody Trusts
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. Her current contract: protective detail for Aldous Wren, a defense-adjacent financier whose enemies are vague and whose paranoia is specific. Jonah notices Wren's staff flinch at certain words. A tail appears outside her gym; she loses it deliberately. Beat: professional calm masking the sense of being watched from inside her own life.

chapters.title: Interest Owed
chapters.summary: Marisol Vega's POV. Introduced in a Nogales safehouse, Marisol decodes the reply she engineered from Jonah's burner. Flashback fragments: a facility, a number instead of a name. She knows exactly what was taken from both of them. Beat: cold purpose warmed by grief for the sister who didn't survive the program.

chapters.title: The Meeting at the Overpass
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. Marisol contacts her directly at a freight overpass, lays out proof: Jonah was 'Candela-7', trained by a program called Meridian that launders operatives through legitimate security firms — including Jonah's own employer. Jonah denies it; her hands shake anyway. Beat: denial colliding with recognition.

chapters.title: What the Training Cost
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV. She explains the debt: Meridian erased recruits' records after activation, leaving them deniable and disposable. Marisol survived extraction; her sister didn't. She wants the archive Wren keeps — the ledger of every Candela operative. Beat: righteous fury tempered by exhaustion.

chapters.title: House Rules
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. Back on the Wren detail, Jonah tests her own reflexes and finds muscle memory she never trained — room-clearing drills, lock work, kill angles. Her partner Deke notices her distraction. Beat: horror at competence she can't account for.

chapters.title: The Ledger Room
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. Recon of Wren's estate reveals a hardened archive behind the wine cellar. Wren catches her lingering too long near it; his gaze lingers a beat too long on her face. Beat: the hunter realizing she may be inventory.

chapters.title: Ghost Protocol, Personal Edition
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV. Marisol pulls DMV, medical, and church records tracing 'Jonah Reyes' backward and finds the identity was fabricated eleven years ago — well-crafted, professionally seeded. Someone built Jonah a life. Beat: tenderness toward a stranger who is also a mirror.

chapters.title: Deke
chapters.summary: Deke Alvarez's POV. Wren's team lead reports Jonah's anomalies to a handler known only as 'Pastor'. We learn Deke is Meridian's eyes inside the detail, and that he genuinely likes Jonah. Beat: loyalty splitting down the middle.

chapters.title: First Blood
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. An ambush on the Wren motorcade — professional, deniable, aimed not at Wren but at extracting Jonah alive. She kills two attackers with efficiency that sickens her. Beat: survival as self-betrayal.

chapters.title: Interrogation of a Memory
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV. Under Marisol's guided recall, Jonah's blocked memories surface in pieces: a white room, a woman reading names aloud, her own voice answering to 'Seven'. Beat: grief arriving before understanding.

chapters.title: The Pastor's Sermon
chapters.summary: Pastor's POV (first appearance). Meridian's operational chief reviews the botched extraction and authorizes 'retirement' protocols for Candela assets. He quotes scripture while ordering deaths. Beat: banality weaponized.

chapters.title: Safehouse Arithmetic
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. Hiding with Marisol, they tally what they know: twelve living Candela operatives, three already dead this month. The math says cleanup has begun. Beat: grim solidarity becoming trust.

chapters.title: The Man She Guards
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. Cross-referencing dates, Jonah realizes Wren wasn't just a client — he attended her intake review. Her employer placed her to guard her own jailer. Beat: betrayal so complete it loops back to dark laughter.

chapters.title: Twelve Names
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV. They contact other survivors. One, Elias Brandt, agrees to meet; another hangs up mid-sentence and vanishes. Beat: hope and attrition in equal measure.

chapters.title: Brandt's Bargain
chapters.summary: Elias Brandt's POV. A Candela operative turned respectable, Brandt offers testimony in exchange for immunity and a new identity — then tips Pastor within the hour. Beat: self-preservation dressed as pragmatism.

chapters.title: The Trap That Wasn't
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. The Brandt meeting is a kill box; Jonah smells it, flips the ambush, and takes a Meridian tech prisoner along with his laptop. Beat: the training finally feeling like hers, not theirs.

chapters.title: What the Laptop Knew
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV. The laptop yields partial archive keys and a schedule: full data purge at Wren's estate in nine days. Everything they need to expose Meridian will exist for nine days only. Beat: the clock starts.

chapters.title: Nine Days
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. Planning montage: entry routes, Wren's rotations, Deke's blind spots. Jonah must go back inside the house that owns her file. Beat: dread converted into discipline.

chapters.title: Deke's Confession
chapters.summary: Deke's POV. Ordered to plant tracking on Jonah, Deke instead warns her obliquely over beers — enough for her to confirm he's the mole, not enough to say sorry. Beat: cowardice and conscience sharing a stool.

chapters.title: The Sister's Grave
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV. Marisol visits her sister's unmarked grave in the desert and makes a promise out loud. Jonah follows and, for the first time, tells someone the whole truth of what she remembers. Beat: mourning as fuel.

chapters.title: Retirement Party
chapters.summary: Pastor's POV. Meridian retires two more Candela assets and moves the purge up four days. Pastor requests Jonah be taken intact — he wants to see what Seven became. Beat: menace without raised voice.

chapters.title: Inside the House
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. Using her legitimate access, Jonah re-enters the Wren estate under a maintenance pretext and maps the archive's biometric locks — discovering the primary key is Wren's heartbeat-pattern ring. Beat: audacity sharpened by terror.

chapters.title: The Ring
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV. Marisol fabricates a pulse-mimic rig from salvage and pharmacy parts. It works twice in testing; the third test fries it. Beat: scrappy desperation, gallows humor.

chapters.title: Wren at Dinner
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren dines with Pastor and reveals he knows an asset is circling the archive — he suspects his own bodyguard. He proposes letting the trap close slowly, to study what Meridian made. Beat: intellectual cruelty.

chapters.title: Day Three: Static
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. Comms compromised; the team splits into cells. Jonah cuts all contact with Marisol to protect her, hating every hour of silence. Beat: loneliness chosen as armor.

chapters.title: Day Four: The Other Operative
chapters.summary: Elias Brandt's POV. Sent to flush Jonah out, Brandt instead finds her and, wracked, gives her the final archive passphrase fragment before Pastor's cleaners reach him. Beat: redemption purchased late and paid in full.

chapters.title: Day Five: Burn Notice
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. Meridian torches Jonah's fabricated identity — bank accounts, licenses, lease. Officially, Jonah Reyes never existed. Unofficially, that frees her. Beat: liberation inside catastrophe.

chapters.title: Day Six: Deke's Choice
chapters.summary: Deke's POV. Ordered to deliver Jonah, Deke delivers a warning shot pattern instead and goes dark, burning his own life to buy her hours. Beat: a small man making one large choice.

chapters.title: Day Seven: The Cellar Key
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. Jonah infiltrates during a Wren gala, lifts the pulse-ring protocol via the mimic rig, and reaches the archive door as alarms trip somewhere above. Beat: breathless precision.

chapters.title: Day Seven: Wren's Study
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Confronted by Jonah at gunpoint, Wren offers partnership — the archive, the network, all of it — if she'll come back to work for him. She sees the man who signed her intake form. Beat: temptation as insult.

chapters.title: The Archive Burns Twice
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. Jonah copies everything, then triggers thermite rather than leave any copy for either side. Wren escapes; she doesn't chase. Beat: principle over vengeance.

chapters.title: Running on Empty
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV. Reunion at the border crossing; Marisol extracts a wounded Jonah through a tunnel she's kept for years. The drives are intact; Jonah isn't quite. Beat: relief braided with damage.

chapters.title: Pastor Closes the Book
chapters.summary: Pastor's POV. With the archive destroyed, Pastor pivots to destroying witnesses. He orders the remaining Candela survivors retired and leaks Jonah's photo to every contractor list in the hemisphere. Beat: the net tightening.

chapters.title: The Distribution Problem
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV. Evidence alone won't win — they need journalists, prosecutors, and other survivors to publish simultaneously before Meridian can disappear them. Marisol builds the network the program never thought to fear: ordinary people. Beat: quiet heroism scaling up.

chapters.title: Eight Survivors
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs, interwoven. Across three states, surviving Candela operatives choose — some testify, some run, one turns coat. The story becomes bigger than its two protagonists. Beat: chorus of the formerly nameless.

chapters.title: The Last Sermon
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. Pastor corners Jonah at the safehouse. She wins the fight but can't execute him; instead she leaves him zip-tied for the arriving federal agents, his own files in their hands. Beat: mercy as the final refusal to be what they made.

chapters.title: Publication Day
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV. The story breaks simultaneously across outlets; Wren is arrested boarding a private jet; hearings are announced. Marisol reads her sister's name into the record. Beat: catharsis, earned and incomplete.

chapters.title: A Name of Her Own
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. Legally dead and newly free, Jonah chooses a name — not Reyes, not Seven — and signs a statement with it. Deke sends a postcard from nowhere. Beat: identity reclaimed as authorship.

chapters.title: A Drop for the Border
chapters.summary: Jonah and Marisol's shared POV, alternating. Months later, they run a two-person firm helping people erase themselves safely — the inverse of Meridian. A new envelope arrives; they look at each other and smile. Beat: survival priced, paid, and worth it.
